newsitem.title: UK: Safeway, Abbey launch banking link.
newsitem.headline: Safeway, Abbey launch banking link.

text.p: Abbey National Plc and supermarkets group Safeway Plc on Thursday launched a partnership which will link Safeway's customer loyalty card with banking services.

The two groups said in a statement that the move will start with the introduction of a household management account using Safeway's ABC Bonus card, to be followed by the introduction of a debit card with overdraft facility, a credit card and a range of other financial services.

The Safeway/Abbey National link follows moves by rival British supermarkets into banking. J. Sainsbury Plc is setting up a bank with Bank of Scotland, while market leader Tesco Plc offers interest payments and overdraft facilities with its customer loyalty card.

The Safeway ABC Bonus card, which gives customers bonus points for shopping in its stores, will be accepted in some 70,000 other outlets which accept the Electron debit card, including C&A, Granada, Lillywhites, Virgin and W.H. Smith, the companies said. Safeway's 5.6 million ABC cardholders will be eligible to apply for a "Bonus' account run by Abbey.

"We have been developing a joint strategy with Safeway for some time and welcome the opportunity to work closely with a leading retailer which has a similar customer focus to our own," Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch said.
Safeway chief executive Colin Smith said, "It is the latest, logical extension of Safeway's customer proposition aimed at making shopping easier for today's families."
